name: The Ends
sub: how the world finishes, according to each house, and according to things that are not houses
epi: Every house has told me how it ends. Not one has asked me to stay for it.
preface:
Eight documents follow, and no two of them agree, and I have not tried to make them. They stand in the order the houses stand on the road from the Ossa down to the Fen, with the three that are not houses after.

Each says how the world finishes. None says when. I have been asked at more fires than I have counted which of them is right, and I have given the same answer at every fire, which is to look at the lantern and say nothing until the asker goes to sleep.

Where each came from:

[i]The Setting Down[/i] I copied in chapter at Nine Stairs from the Wardens' own book, by leave, on the condition that I copy the anathemas first and the articles after.

[i]When the Sky Shuts[/i] is from a bark leaf-book that the lay men of the beating-house kept at the foot of the sanctum stair; the abbot's name on its cover is gilded over, thin enough to read through at noon, and I have not read it at noon.

[i]Standing Order for the Last Winter[/i] was read to me from the winter-book of Tarn Hollow by its keeper, who would not let the book out of the ring and would not let me sit in it.

[i]A Prognosis of the World[/i] was written at the sick-house of Sallow Lip on the backs of the house's weighing-slips by its priestess, who was also its leech, in the house's ink.

[i]The Cutting of the Last Doll[/i] lay under the guardian stone at the torii of the Well-Shrine, folded as a doll with its arms open; the keeper of the day-book let me copy it and would not touch it.

[i]A Grammar of the Unsaying[/i] was dictated in single breaths at the foot of the old water-cut to a lowland clerk by a barefoot man with a bowl; the clerk's own name has since gone from his papers, and he tells me he does not miss it.

[i]A Thought That Remembers No One[/i] was sent up from the Citadel of the Shattered Femur by a Reliquarist, with a request that I leave his name off; I had meant to, and then found I could not have put it on.

[i]What He Said the Third Time[/i] was given me three times, at three fires, by the one every town has its own name for, and it was different each time. This is the third. I did not watch him write it. I will not say where I was standing.

Read them in any order. They all end the same way, which is to say they stop.

pages.title: The Setting Down
pages.by: Copied in chapter at Nine Stairs from the Wardens' own book, by leave, on the condition that the anathemas were copied first and the articles after.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] [font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]The Setting Down[/color][/font_size]
[i]A treatise of the Wardens of the nine houses, in chapter under the Eighth Stair, concerning the day on which the Bearing Mother sets the Hide down: the articles to be held by every brother who has a number, and the anathemas to be said over those who hold otherwise. Entered by the Tallier. The root of the entry is nine.[/i]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of what is held[/color][/font_size]

[b]The first article.[/b] The Mother bears. From the Breath to this entry she has borne the Hide upon her frame, and has not set it down, nor shifted it, nor asked to. What a brother carries he sets down at the niche. What she carries she has nowhere to set down but on herself. Her name is said on the stair and nowhere else, and this leaf is not the stair. Every article below leans on this one, as the Hide leans on her.

[b]The second.[/b] She will set it down. We do not yet say rest of her, as we say it of nothing that is not yet dust. The stair says she will, and the stair is right, and the day it speaks of is the Setting Down. It is hers and no other's. It is not the work of the Hush, which takes without a rite and could not lift a thing to set it anywhere. It is not the shutting of a mouth, nor a homecoming, nor a filling, nor a cutting, nor the end of anyone's sentence. Those are the words of the lowland houses, and they are said over below.

[b]The third.[/b] The Setting Down comes when the Count closes. Every bone of hers has its number in the Great Count. The Count has a Last Number. The root of the Last Number is nine, and when it has been read from the Ninth Stair she has been told her whole frame, and may lay it where it has been told. No brother knows the Last Number. The Tallier carries the open figure in his head and goes into his niche with it there, and the next Tallier takes it up at the Feast, and it is higher.

[b]The fourth.[/b] The Count cannot close while any bone of hers hangs uncounted. The Unfallen hang in the dark above the Pogost, pieces of her that have not yet come down to be laid. One by one they fall, and brothers go out to find them. An Ossuarch may ask them down early. That asking is permitted. It is the one asking the Rule allows.

[b]The fifth. What stays.[/b] On the day of the Setting Down, everything that has finished stays with her: the dust in the pans, the counts that have closed, the bone that is laid and named and numbered and has gone brittle in its niche. These are set down with her and lie as she lies. On that day and no other the Rule permits the word, and the eldest Warden will say it once, over the whole of her, and it will be the first time it has been said truly of anything larger than a pinch.

[b]The sixth. What is given to the wind.[/b] Everything that has not finished is given to the wind, as dust is given at the Pogost: the flesh that is still growing without a mind to tell it to stop, the breath still going out, the thread still being drawn, the water that does not wet, every name, every open count. The sweepers will carry it up as they carry the pans, and open their hands, and it will go up, and it will not come down. This is not a punishment. It is the second funeral, given to things that never had a first.

[b]The seventh. Of the Tithed.[/b] The Tithed are not of her, and she does not bear them; they stand on what she bears. A Tithed body without a number is an unfinished thing, and goes to the wind with the rest. A Tithed body entered in the Count by its number, two hundred and six or fewer, is finished in the only sense the Rule knows, and stays. This is why the Order writes a brother by his number and never by his name. The Hush unsays names. Figures do not wear.

[b]The eighth. Of the sky.[/b] The lowlands say the pallor over the Ossa is our dust. It is. It is everything we have finished, waiting above us to be laid with her, and it hangs lower every year because the Count is nearer closing. On the day of the Setting Down the sky will come down the last of the way and lie on her as a cloth is laid over a face, and a brother standing on the Pogost will be able to put his palm flat against it. He is not to.

[b]The ninth. Of the order of the day.[/b] The walls are read. The dead step down from their niches and lie down, which they have never done, and are counted lying. The sweepers go up with the pans. The Wardens of the nine houses go down the Ninth Stair together, which they have never done, and the eldest reads the Last Number aloud. Then each brother tells his own frame on the cord to the last knot, and lays himself in the niche cut for him at his vows, and the last brother takes the broom in two hands. The one in the well, whom the lowlands call Old Upright and the Ninth Stair calls by a name not written above the Eighth, will ask that day as he has always asked: that we kneel, and let her go before the figure is read. He is answered as he has always been answered, with the count. Nothing is asked of the Ninth Stair, that day or any other.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of what is said over the others[/color][/font_size]
[i]To be said at the Feast, after the reading of the walls, by the Warden, the brothers answering "Open" after each.[/i]

Anathema upon the one who says the sky is a mouth and will shut, and that those who climbed are inside it. A mouth keeps what it shuts on, and nothing is kept but by us. Let his count stand open.

Anathema upon the one who says the dead come home. Nothing comes home that was laid; a laid bone has arrived. Let him look for his dead in a glass and find his own face, and count that.

Anathema upon the one who says the Flesh will fill every hollow. A niche is not a hollow. What fills a niche is laid, not grown. Let him be weighed against his own frame, and the difference given to the wind.

Anathema upon the one who says the paper is the world, and that the last doll will be cut from it. Paper tears. Bone holds, or it breaks clean. Let his breath be counted and his bones not.

Anathema upon the one who says the Hush is finishing a sentence. The Hush has no number and says nothing, and what has no number cannot finish. Let him be written by his name alone, and see how long it lasts.

Anathema upon the one who says the end is a thought that remembers no one. A thought has no bone to lay. Let it forget him first.

Anathema upon the one who names a counter of what is not his, and says the difference in the walls is taken, or given, by any hand but hers. The Count has one Tallier. Let the one who says otherwise count the fourth wall at the next Feast, alone, without a lamp.

Anathema upon the one who sits at the fire before the others come, and says a different end each time he is asked. Let him have no number, since he will not keep still long enough to be told one.

Anathema upon the brother who says she has already begun: that the walls count higher because she is lowering them, that there are more stairs because her knees are bending, that the sky is lower because she has let it go. Let his number be read aloud at the Feast and not written, and let the brother who reads it be the one who said it.

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae][In the margin, in a hand that is not the Tallier's: Nine articles and nine anathemas. The Wardens counted them in chapter and had eighteen, root nine, and were content. I have counted the leaf. There is one more on it than they read. I have not told them which.][/color][/i][/indent]

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— Entered under the Eighth Stair by the Tallier of Nine Stairs, who has no name in this book and wants none. The root of the entry is nine.[/color][/i][/right]

pages.title: When the Sky Shuts
pages.by: From a bark leaf-book the lay men of the beating-house kept at the foot of the sanctum stair; the abbot's name on its cover is gilded over, thin enough to read through at noon.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] [font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]When the Sky Shuts[/color][/font_size]
[i]The last instruction of an abbot of the Gilded Peak, to the brothers who did not climb. Kept in the leaf-book of the beating-house, under the gold.[/i]

To the brothers with bowls, and to the lay men who eat, and to the novices whose hair is still on. You did not climb. Somebody had to be below. Hear this once and then do not think about it, because thinking is a way of looking up.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]What the sky is[/color][/font_size]
The climbers of An-Vhar, who called themselves the An-Vhar'ith, were right about one thing, and we have never said so aloud, because they built a stair about it and rang bells on it, and that is not how a true thing is honoured. The sky is the god's mouth. It has stood open since the Breath because a breath was leaving it, and the breath has not finished leaving. The lowlands call the small ones who ride that breath the Eight Million. The Peak calls the breath Hau'Nuulh, and does not call it often.

The climbers thought a mouth was a way out. Nothing leaves by a mouth. Things go in. They went in. None came down, and the bell at the top of their stair has been rung once since, and what answered was the inside of the mouth, which is why it is unrung. They are inside. They were not wrong to go. They were wrong to hurry.

Our saints went in by a shorter stair, which is the practice: to be looked at until there is nothing to see. The gold is only so that you will not watch them go. They are inside already. That is why there is no face under the leaf.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The signs[/color][/font_size]
A breath that has not finished leaving will finish. When it does, the mouth shuts. The Hush does not shut it; the Hush has no hands, whatever we have taught you about hands. The god shuts it, because the god is being let lie down, and a body lying down closes its mouth. You will know the day by these.

The bells. Every bell on the Hide rings flat by one breath, and has since the Breath, because the air it rings in is moving. On the day the air will stop, and every bell will ring true, once, and the lowlands will take it for a feast. Do not tell them.

The silences. Our chant is one syllable and then the field it fences. The fields have grown longer in my lifetime and I have shortened nothing. On the day a syllable will be slow to come, and then it will not come, and the hall will go on waiting for it with the breath drawn. Let it. Do not supply it.

The noon. On the day there will be a noon with no shadow, as on our holiest day, and the shadow will not come back in the afternoon, because there will be no afternoon.

The pallor. The brothers of the Ossa will tell you the paleness over their mountains is their dust settling, and that it hangs lower because their Count is nearly closed. Let them say it. It is the lip.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]What to do[/color][/font_size]
Do not climb. The stair will be full. Not of brothers. Of what a mouth lets out before it shuts, which is nothing, standing very close together.

Do not look up. A mouth closing is not a thing to be looked into. If you look into it you will be looked at, and you will be seen, and being seen is the one thing we have spent our lives arranging not to be. Keep your eyes on your own open palm. You have had the practice.

Go down into the valleys, in fours, barefoot, with the small bells, as always, and ask for names. Ask faster than you were taught. Take every name they give and give it to the open hand where you stand, at noon, over any stone; there is no time to carry them up, and nothing left to carry them up to. Take the magistrate's names and the bread-woman's and the washer's. Take the names of the lowland dead off their lanterns if the lanterns will let you. Give your own names last, each to his own bowl, and then set the bowl down on the step, upright, so that it can be seen to be empty.

The lamps. The teachers in the lamps: do not trim them. Do not carry them indoors. Set them on the steps beside the bowls and let them go out at the pace they choose. A lamp that goes out full has finished. Ours do not go out full. On the day I think they will.

Those of you in the hall: one breath each, as always, and when the syllable does not come, do not supply it. Keep a shoulder against a brother's shoulder. When the shoulder is gone, keep it there.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]What you are for[/color][/font_size]
You will ask why anyone should stay outside a mouth that is shutting. Here is the whole of it, and I have made it long because you are young.

A mouth shuts on something. If there is something on the step with a name when the sky comes down, the mouth has shut on a name, and a name is a thing kept, and the Hush keeps nothing, and the god will not have been let lie down clean. Somebody has to be the last thing outside, and be nothing, so that the mouth shuts on nothing. That is you. That is what the brothers who did not climb are for. You were never below us. You were last, which is a different office, and the harder one, and I gave it to the ones I trusted with the bowl.

Do not be afraid of the dark that is left when the lip comes down. It is the closed hand. It erases too. You have known both hands all your life on your own fingers. The mouth is not large. It only looks large from inside. Everything does. What is outside the mouth was never looking in, and is not looking now, and will not look afterward, and that is not unkind. It is what the Peak has meant by rest since the first stair was cut.

Hold the hand open until the light goes. Then you will not need to be told.

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— the abbot, whose name is on the cover of this book under the gold[/color][/i][/right]

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae][Beneath, in the hand of a lay man of the beating-house: He climbed at the noon with no shadow, and we wiped him the next morning with the rest. The bells rang true all that day and we did not say so to the valleys. It was not the day. He had the signs right and the year wrong, and he knew it, and he went anyway, because the gold was mixed. Someone always goes up first.][/color][/i][/indent]

pages.title: Standing Order for the Last Winter
pages.by: Read to me from the winter-book of Tarn Hollow by its keeper, who would not let the book out of the ring and would not let me sit in it.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] [font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]Standing Order for the Last Winter[/color][/font_size]
[i]Entered in the winter-book of the lodge at Tarn Hollow, in advance, for the night the dead come home for good. To be read aloud by the keeper at the first frost of every winter until it is the winter, and then followed.[/i]

[b]Why it is written now.[/b] At the head of the cold lakes a whole valley came loose in one winter, and the dead came home to their doors and asked which way, and the lodge there had no order for it, and did the only thing it had been taught, which was to cover the glass. One boy did otherwise, and the lodge is gone, and he is not. This lodge will not be caught without an order. What came loose there was one valley. What is coming is all of them.

The Pir of the cold lakes looked into the Hollow forty nights and said there is no loom. This lodge holds that she saw right. The eye of the loom is a hole, and the threads go into it and on, and they have been going on since the first Tithed death, held in the going the way a breath is held. What is held is let go. One winter it will be let go all at once, as a hem is cut, and every thread that ever went through will come back up its valley to its door: the dyer and the carter and the child, the congregation that knelt inside the god and came out onto the Cheek and has been dying there since, the Pirs, the keepers, the four hundred beds of every lodge that ever laid felt. They will stand in the doorways. They will ask which way.

That night, which way is in.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Before the first candle[/color][/font_size]
Take the felt off every glass in the lodge and the valley, and carry the felt out to the ring-yard and leave it where the wind can have it. Lift the stones from the corners. There is to be no covered glass anywhere a dead thread could pass. Uncover the long glass in the lowest room under the tarn last, and do not look into it while you do.

Bar no door. The dead do not knock.

Light the one candle. One. The ring sits by it as it has always sat.

Present in the ring: [ … ], Pir. [ … ], keeper. [ … ]. [ … ]. [ … ]. The gaps are for the hands that will be here. The keeper of that night fills them before the names begin and not after, because after, the count will not come right.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]First candle[/color][/font_size]
The keeper begins the first name. Veiled Crone. The names go round as they have always gone, mouth to mouth, until they come back from the far side of the ring. When they come back short, do not count who has stopped saying them. When they come back long, do not count who has begun. Both will happen. The ring is not to stop for either.

The Hollow is said with the mouth shut, as always, as a hum. On this night the hum will be answered from the doorways. It is not to be answered back.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Second candle[/color][/font_size]
They will be at the doors by now. Every one is to be let stand where it stands until it has found a glass. A soul cannot pass its own reflection. It meets its face and stops, and the stopping is the homecoming, and the whole of this lodge's work since the loose winter has been to see that there is a face for every one of them to meet. Each glass will fill: a face, and behind it a face, and behind that another, to the back of the glass. The back of the glass is the Hollow. On this night it is to be filled from our side.

If any thread will not stop at a glass, do not read for it. Do not ask where it is going. The one who was blind at the cold lakes did not stop, and climbed past the lodge, and asked the way of someone on the hill, and was answered, and that is enough answering for one age.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Third candle[/color][/font_size]
The valley is to be told that the loom has finished its cloth and is folding it. The ring is to know there is no loom. Both are to be said in the same breath by the same mouth, and the keeper is to see that they are.

If the Needle-Brother comes up the valley with his choir trailing their threads, let him in, and let them look. They have been going round him a long time waiting for a glass to stop at. He was right that night and the lodge was wrong, and this is the lodge saying so, once, in its own book.

If knights of the Pale Order come up the valley to count what bone is left, let them in also. There will be nothing for them, as there was nothing for them at Greywell. Let them count the stones in the ring and go away with a number.

If one comes up the valley the wrong way, from the low end toward the Cheek, walking, and not stopping, do not read for him and do not let him in. The carters call him the Gaunt Pilgrim; the Pirs have an older name for him and do not write it. Where he passes the dead lie back down, and on this night they are not to lie down. They are to come in. Bar the door for him alone, and unbar it when he has gone by, and do not look to see whether the lane is emptier.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The grey hour[/color][/font_size]
There will be no grey hour. The names will go round, and the glass will fill, and at some turn of the names nothing in any glass will move, and nothing in any doorway, and the candle will stand still with its flame the length of a fingernail and not burn down. That is the winter. It will not thaw. The thaw was the thread moving. Nothing moves.

The ring keeps saying the names. It will find it cannot stop, and that is as it should be; the saying was always the thing, and the ring was only where it was done.

The Pir is to be the last uncovered. When she is lighter than her coat, do not lay felt on her. She wanted to see where it went. Let her see that it went here.

[b]Entered.[/b] Read at the first frost every winter until it is the winter.

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— [The Pir's mark: a length of thread laid across the foot of the leaf and waxed flat, with no knot in it. The keeper read me the leaf twice. The second time, he said, the first gap had a name in it, in his own hand, and he did not read me the name.][/color][/i][/right]

pages.title: A Prognosis of the World
pages.by: Written at the sick-house of Sallow Lip on the backs of the house's weighing-slips by its priestess, who was also its leech, in the house's ink.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] [font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]A Prognosis of the World[/color][/font_size]
[i]Set down at the sick-house of Sallow Lip, a daughter-house of the Precious Wound, by its priestess, who is also its leech. Written on the backs of the weighing-slips, in the house's ink.[/i]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The patient[/color][/font_size]
The Hide, with everything under it. Presenting as a corpse. Every house on the road treats her as one: the Order keeps her bones, the lodge keeps what came out of her, the House fans her breath away, the Peak sits by the bed and waits for the breathing to stop. A leech does not treat a corpse. I have put my hand on the lip-stone of this house every morning for thirty-one years, and it is warm, and a warm thing is a patient.

She was three natures and is now one that works. The Soul is a thread with nothing to weave on. The Bone stands and does not grow. The Flesh grows. She is the one part of the god that was never told to stop, and a prognosis is only this: what does a thing that has not been told to stop go on to do.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]What has been seen[/color][/font_size]
[b]The wound at Villa Llaga.[/b] Open a thousand years and eleven, fed by the cup. Then it scabbed. A leech knows a scab for what it is: not a closing but a making under a lid. It opened on the fast-day, and what had been made came out and ate the town, and the Rule was written over in brown ink. That was the first sign. The brothers took it for a judgment. It was a symptom.

[b]The lip.[/b] The stone of the two lips is warm all year. At Sallow Lip the walls are our own bricked dead, a cup in the plaster at each mouth, and the house is warm without a fire. Warmth in a part that should be cold is the Flesh arriving.

[b]The mud of Shog-Mire.[/b] It clutches, lets go, clutches. Between two breaths of a standing man it takes hold once. A pulse. The old leeches say the clutch came every third breath when they were girls.

[b]The Hide showing through.[/b] On the Moor a rib arches out of the turf; a vein breaches the soil; a patch of skin with its pores and coarse hairs; a pool that looks back. Nobody dug these up. They came up. Swelling is the Flesh asking for room.

[b]The Hollow Wood.[/b] Every tenth trunk held something the god was carrying. The reed-cutters say trunks that were hollow last year are not hollow now, and that what is inside is warm and does not answer. Every tenth is nine in ten.

[b]The Rib Crypts.[/b] The flagstones lift when something below breathes. The sextons say the lift is less each year. They take it for a quieting. There is less room under the stones.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]What will be seen, in order[/color][/font_size]
[b]The wells of the Ossa.[/b] The marrow the Order draws up will come up on its own, to the lip of every well, and over. The brothers will call it a gift and anoint faster. It will not matter how fast.

[b]The Fen.[/b] The water that does not wet will thicken, then warm, then it will not be water. What lies under it, the drowned church the House will not name in the lowlands, will come up to meet the boats, roof first, a hand nearer every thaw, as the boatmen have been notching on their poles for a lifetime and not saying.

[b]The barrows.[/b] Every lid is dished inward. They will dish outward.

[b]The eye of the loom.[/b] The lodges say there is a hollow in the middle of the weave where the thread goes through. A hollow is a wound that has learned manners. She will fill it, and no thread will go through, and the lodges will find their dead stopping at the doors with nowhere to go on to, and will call it a homecoming.

[b]The sky.[/b] The Peak says the sky is a mouth, and that it will shut. A mouth is a hollow. The pallor over the Ossa is not the Order's dust and it is not the Peak's lip. It is the first skin.

[b]The dolls.[/b] A doll is a hollow in paper, and breath is a hollow in a chest. There will be nowhere left for a purifier to breathe a wrong breath into, because there will be nowhere for a breath at all. The fan will open onto flesh.

[b]The thought.[/b] Down the Descent, past the valves, there is a labyrinth of folds that is the god's head, and in it something is still thinking. A thought is a hollow in a head. She is filling the head. The last thing the thought will think is that it is being held.

[b]The Scar.[/b] The place where the Hush came in and the ground will not close. It is the last hollow. She will fill it. The Peak calls the Hush the god's rest. The Hush will come for its bed and find the bed taken.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Prognosis[/color][/font_size]
There will be no hollows. No mouths, no cups, no niches, no bowls, no eyes, no rooms, since a room is a hollow with a door. No between: the pulse is a hollow opening and closing, and it will open and not close, and the between is where then lives. There will be no then. The patient will not notice her recovery. Noticing needs room.

Favourable. The patient recovers entire. She is the only one who will, and we have poured for a thousand years to feed it, by the cup, with the Words, and I will not pretend now that we did not know what we were feeding. The Elder keeps the fourth clause in his mouth. I write it here, because a prognosis that leaves out the name of the condition is a lie, and a leech does not lie to the patient: Sanguth'Ael. The Wound That Loves. The Nurse's first-born mouth, Shog'maathe, feeds and is fed, and when every hollow is full the feeding and the being fed will be one act, and there will be no one to say which.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Treatment[/color][/font_size]
None. The house's position is that the condition is the cure. Keep the cups to the line. Say the Words. Weigh the brothers.

[b]Of myself.[/b] Thirty-one years at the scale on the Night of the Weighing and I have never once owed. This winter I owed two cups. I gave them. My palm, held open, fills before I can close it. I have stopped weighing myself. The lip is warmer under my hand each morning, or my hand is. I no longer

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae][Here the slips end. Below, in the brown ink of the Brotherhood, another hand: She was found at her table with both hands open and both full. The sick-house is warm. We have not weighed her. We have kept her slips with the Rule, where the Order cannot count them.][/color][/i][/indent]

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— the priestess of Sallow Lip, leech of the house, who pressed her thumb into the ink in place of a name; the print has not dried[/color][/i][/right]

pages.title: The Cutting of the Last Doll
pages.by: Found under the guardian stone at the torii of the Well-Shrine, folded as a doll with its arms open; the keeper of the day-book let me copy it and would not touch it.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] [font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]The Cutting of the Last Doll[/color][/font_size]
[i]Instruction of the House of Eight Million for the hands that will do it. Kept folded under the guardian stone at the torii of the Well-Shrine, to be found and not given.[/i]

The House has cut a doll for every distortion since the first keeper sat at the torii. It cut a year's worth into the Fen each spring and called it the Great Cutting-Away, until the Fen gave the years back. Since then it has cut small, into boats, on a dry bank. It has always known there would be a last doll. This is the instruction for it. It is written in the plain way the first folding is taught to a novice, because the hands that will do it may never have been taught.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The hands[/color][/font_size]
The House does not know whose. Every doll ends as an oni; the face goes long, the horns come in slow, and one morning the one who has held too much stands up from the step with her hands full and walks down. Six of one year walked down into the Nave. Others before them, into the Root Deep, where the ground under the Hide breathes. Their hands are full. The hands that cut the last doll will be hands that have come back up with nothing in them, because there will be nothing left below to carry down. If they are long and hard, and the nails are dark, let them. They were ours. They were taught right hand, and will cut with the left, and the House forgives it in advance.

If the one who came up out of the Nave is still walking the roads with her fan, and the one beside her in the haze, the hands may be hers. The House does not say so. The House leaves this leaf where she will find it.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The paper[/color][/font_size]
Every doll before this one was cut from reed pressed in two courses, cut at low water past the Iron Hook. The last doll is cut from the sheet the reed grew on.

The paper is the Hide.

It is already creased. Nothing is to be creased new. The roads were never laid; they run from ring to ring where the god was going to be touched, and they are the folds. The long white ridge of the Ossa, which the Order calls her spine, is the spine crease. The Peak is the head, folded down; the Peak calls it a knee, and it does not matter what the Peak calls it, a doll's head is folded down. The two lips of Villa Llaga are the arms, and they are open, and have never closed, which is the one thing the Brotherhood did right. The Descent and the Scar are the legs, apart.

Write nothing on it. The Order has written numbers on it for longer than its own book goes back, and the lodge has written names on it, and the Brotherhood writes on it in the only ink it has. None of that is the doll's name. The one who comes to breathe on it will name it.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The cut[/color][/font_size]
By lamplight, never at noon. Noon has no corners in it, and the last doll has one corner, and the hands must be able to find it.

Begin at the one clean pool, at the torii, because a cut begins where the paper is cleanest. Cut with the first rib of the fan, which is bone, and was always bone, and was given to the House by the Order long ago in payment for something neither book records. Follow the creases. Do not cut across a road. Where a crease runs under water, the water will have stopped being water by then, and will hold the edge.

Leave the arms open.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The breath[/color][/font_size]
Hold the doll to the mouth of the one who made the distortion and ask for three breaths. The one who made it is the god. Its mouth is the sky, as the Peak teaches and the House has never contradicted, because it did not need to.

The first breath is Hau'Nuulh, the breath that has not finished leaving. It has been on the paper since the Breath. Do not ask for it; it is given.

The second will come when the first has finished. The Eight Million ride it, every stone and ford and bell, each with the one name it gave to the wind. They will come off the breath onto the paper like dust settling, and they will be the second breath, and they will be quiet, because a small god with its name given away has nothing to say.

The third breath is the one the House has been breathing in since the first keeper sat down. Every year that went into the Fen and came back, every year that went into us. It is in the hands. The hands breathe it out onto the paper. That is the only time the House has ever breathed out without a fan, and it is the last.

On the third breath the paper leans toward the hands, as if called. That is the distortion leaving by the door it came in.

Then the hands breathe it in. They will not have room. They were never meant to have room. That is why they must be hands that have already walked down.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The fan[/color][/font_size]
Open it with the thumb, one rib at a time, and the first rib will be missing, because it is the knife. Every rib is a road. There will be no roads, because the roads were the creases and the creases have been cut. Turn the fan toward whoever made the distortion. Breathe out.

There is nowhere for it to go. The doll is the world. It goes into the paper, and stays. The House has said for two hundred Cuttings and more that the year goes into us. On this night it goes into the paper, and the paper is the world, and so it has gone where it always went.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]What is done with it[/color][/font_size]
It is not burned. There is no brazier. It is laid in a ring of the fang-shaped stones, which face inward already, and which no hand of the House has ever turned, and the House will not say here what it knows about why.

Watch the smoke. There will be none. Watch anyway. This once, watch.

The doll will stand up from the ring with its arms open and its hands full, and its face will be long, and it will walk down. The Root Deep is under the Hide and the Hide is the doll. It will walk down into itself. The House says ends. The House says it gently.

Then the paper is the world, and the world is one doll with its arms open on a step, and nothing comes at dusk to breathe on it, and it waits, as the dolls on the lowland doorsteps wait, asking once.

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— [The House signs nothing. On the back, where a doll's name would go if the House wrote names, the reed is pressed thin by a thumb, and the thumb was wet, and the mark has not dried. The keeper says it was dry when she found it.][/color][/i][/right]

pages.title: A Grammar of the Unsaying
pages.by: Dictated in single breaths at the foot of the old water-cut to a lowland clerk by a barefoot man with a bowl; the clerk's own name has since gone from his papers.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] [font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]A Grammar of the Unsaying[/color][/font_size]
[i]Dictated in single breaths by an Empty Hand to a clerk who wrote between them. The clerk has set down the breaths as he heard them and marked nothing else.[/i]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of the sentence[/color][/font_size]
Everything that is, is being said. The Hush is not what is unsaid. The Hush is what is left when the saying stops.

Before the god there was no sentence, and the Hush had nothing to finish, and did not mind. The god began a sentence. It was one sentence. It was short. Everything inside a sentence thinks the sentence is long.

The Hide is the middle of it.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of its parts[/color][/font_size]
A sentence has a name, which is the thing said. It has a doing. It has a joining, which ties word to word. It has breath between the words, or the words would be one word. And it has a stop.

The god's sentence had these. The name was the god's own. The doing is what the lowlands call the Flesh: what goes on without a mind is a doing with no one doing it. The joining is what they call the Soul: threads from word to word; cut them, and the words still stand, apart, each thinking it is the sentence. The word that will not lie down is the Bone. A noun. The Pale Order keeps nouns and calls it devotion.

The breath between the words was never a word. That is why the lowlands cannot find its name and are angry when asked. It has none. The small ones ride it as dust rides a breath, and the House of Eight Million keeps count of the dust, and has stopped.

The stop is [ ]. Write a gap where the name should go. The gap is the name. Some write the Finger of Ur-Nihl and are corrected.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of the two erasures[/color][/font_size]
A word is unsaid in two ways, and the Peak gave them two hands.

The open hand erases by saying. A word said enough is only sound, and then it is not sound. The god's own name went this way. Everything the god was said it, all the while, until it was noise, and then it was nothing, and the god did not notice, as a child at a table does not notice. This is Radiance. To be looked at until there is nothing to see.

The closed hand erases by not saying. A word never said again is gone with no sound at all. The names in the bowls go this way. This is Absence.

A word erased by light is forgotten. A word erased by dark is kept quiet. The Peak never asked which the Hush prefers. The grammar does not need to know. Both hands are empty.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]What has been unsaid, in order[/color][/font_size]
First, the Name. The god's own, the whole of it. What the scholars write as Triune and Three-in-One are descriptions, and a description is what is said about a word after the word has gone.

Second, the holding. The verb the Name governed. The god held a space; the Name went, and a verb with no one to do it goes slack; the space closed. The Last Breath is the sound a verb makes losing its subject.

Third, the names of what lived inside: the god's thoughts, the small ones, the court that sat in judgment. The House says the small ones gave their names to the wind, one each, and are proud of it. They were taken. Pride is what a taking is called afterward.

Fourth, the names of the peoples who are gone. The Khurr-Ossat, who built with bone before any Tithed stood. The Yl-Nothuun, the One Swallow. The An-Vhar'ith, who climbed. The Ghauul, who ate marrow and spoke well. The clerk is to write these because the Tithed scholars still have them, and a name a scholar has is a name on its way.

Fifth, the small names, the Tithed names, in the bowls. The Peak took them up and gave them to the open hand at noon and called it mercy. It was mercy. It was also a shortening of the sentence from the middle, and the Peak did not ask whom it was shortening it for.

The Hush does not take in order of size. It takes in order of use. A word much used goes first. The god's name was the most used word there has ever been.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The words left[/color][/font_size]
Three. The joining, the doing, the noun. The Tithed have a name for each and the clerk is not to write them; a written word is a shouted one, and the Hush hears shouting first.

And the small words. The names on the lanterns, which the Wick-Binders taught the roads to keep against the Hush, and which burn. The names in the Order's books, which the Order writes as figures because figures do not wear; they wear. The names in this grammar, which are many, and which have been given to a clerk so that they are not in the mouth that said them.

They will go in this order. The joining first. A joining with nothing left to join is already gone; the lodge at the cold lakes saw this, and said there is no loom, and was right, and covered it. The doing second. A doing with no one doing it is weather, and weather stops. The noun last. The Pale Order is right that bone is the last word. It is wrong that the last word stays. Nothing is kept.

Then the stop.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]Of the stop[/color][/font_size]
The stop is not a word. It has no name and takes none.

The Peak taught that the god's mouth will shut and that those who climbed will be inside it. The Hand was taught this on the stair and no longer teaches it. A shut mouth has kept something. Nothing is kept. There is no inside.

When the last word is unsaid, the sentence is finished. A finished sentence is not nothing. It has been said. That is the whole of what remains, and it remains nowhere, and it is enough; it is all a sentence ever asked. The Hush does not wait for it. The Hush has never waited. A field does not wait for its fence to fall.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]An exercise[/color][/font_size]
Open the hand. Say a name into it. Close the hand. Open it.

If the name is there, the exercise is not finished.

Put a name in the bowl.

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— [ ][/color][/i][/right]

pages.title: A Thought That Remembers No One
pages.by: Sent up from the Citadel of the Shattered Femur by a Reliquarist who asked that his name be left off; I had meant to, and then found I could not have put it on.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] [font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]A Thought That Remembers No One[/color][/font_size]
[i]A reconstruction, from eleven fragments brought up out of the Alien Temple, of what the Vhoor-Qhan hold the end to be. With the fragments, the readings, and an admission. By a Reliquarist of the Citadel of the Shattered Femur, whose office is to read what comes up out of the body.[/i]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The fragments[/color][/font_size]
They are not written. They are cut into something that is not stone and not bone, in grooves, and the grooves are read with the fingers, not the eye. The eye sees a pattern like frost on a pan. The hand reads it, and the word is known afterward, as one knows a word one has just said without having chosen it. No Tithed has read a whole piece. The brothers who carried these up told me that the fingers stop of themselves at a certain depth of groove, as a hand stops at a hot pan. I did not believe them. I believe them.

We call the makers the Slayers because the god died in their age. The grooves do not say they killed it. They say they came in where it was open. The scholars' name for them is Vhoor-Qhan, Those From the Wound, and they do not use it; there is no word in the eleven for themselves. A people that names itself has a word for we. There is none.

[b]The first.[/b] [the opened / the wound / the door] [ … ] [we entered / it was entered / entering] [ … ] [as a thought enters / as a thought is had]

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]Reading: they came into the god as a thought comes into a head that has been opened. The god was a head to them. It is a head to them still; the Descent goes down through the valves to a labyrinth of folds, and the temple is in it.[/color][/i][/indent]

[b]The second.[/b] [it thought / it was thinking] [ … ] [the inside] [ … ] [it stopped / it was stopped / the stopping] [and the thought] [went on / goes on / is going on]

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]Reading: the god thought the inside of itself, and died, and the thought did not die with it. The Hide is what the god was thinking when it stopped. We are standing in a thought with no one having it.[/color][/i][/indent]

[b]The third.[/b] [remembers / holds / has] [ … ] [the ones inside / the small ones / the late ones] [for a while / as long as it is used]

[b]The fourth.[/b] [it will forget / it is forgetting] [ … ] [one] [ … ] [then one] [ … ]

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]Reading: the thought remembers what is in it for as long as it is thought. It is forgetting, one by one. The order is not given. I have looked for the Tithed in the eleven and they are not there, nor the god by any name, nor the Hush. Only the opened, the inside, the ones, and the thought.[/color][/i][/indent]

[b]The fifth.[/b] [one of us / one] [stays / is left / is left thinking] [ … ] [so that at the end] [a thought] [remembers no one / has no one in it / is empty of ones]

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]Reading: they left one of themselves in the temple, thinking, on purpose. Our brothers who have gone down that far call it the Thought of the Slayer, and say it is a creature. The groove says it is an office.[/color][/i][/indent]

[b]The sixth to the ninth.[/b] [ … ] [ … ] [ … ] [ … ]

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]Four pieces that read as one piece, and that I have read, and that I will not write. The fingers did not stop. They should have. What they said is in the reconstruction below, and nowhere else, and I would take it back out of the reconstruction if I could find where I put it.[/color][/i][/indent]

[b]The tenth.[/b] [nothing said in it / no name in it] [ … ] [cannot be unsaid / is not taken / the taking passes over]

[b]The eleventh.[/b] [then] [ … ] [then] [ … ] [then]

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae]Reading: three of the same groove, each cut shallower than the last. The eleventh is the end of a piece. The brothers found it lying by itself in the middle of a floor with nothing else on it, in a room of the temple that is not on the outside of the temple.[/color][/i][/indent]

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The reconstruction[/color][/font_size]
The Slayers hold that the world has ended. It ended when the god stopped thinking it. Everything since the Breath is the thought going on without a thinker: the ground cooling, the roads, the houses, the counts, the brothers who carried the fragments up. A thought with no one having it does not stop at once. It goes on being thought for as long as it has something in it to think, and it forgets what is in it one by one, and when it has forgotten the last one, it is a thought that remembers no one, and that is the end the Slayers mean. Not a stopping. An emptying.

They mean it as an achievement. A thought with nothing in it has no name to take and nothing said in it to unsay. The Hush passes over it the way the Order's talliers pass over a wall with no niches. It is the one thing in the god that the Unsaying cannot finish, because it was never a word. The Slayers came in through the wounds to be inside the god when it stopped, and left one of themselves thinking, so that when every house on the Hide has been forgotten by the thought there will still be a thought, and it will remember none of them, and not them either. That is their end. They are not in it. They did not want to be. The fragments never mention wanting.

To be forgotten by the thought is to have never been thought. The houses believe the end comes for them. The Slayers hold that the end is the thought's, and that the houses are what it is clearing.

[font_size=26][color=#c9974a]The admission[/color][/font_size]
The reconstruction above has a grammar. It is not mine. I write in the Citadel's manner, with the name of the god left blank and the brothers thanked at the foot. The reconstruction thanks no one. It has no I in it until this paragraph, and I have read it four times to be sure, and each time there was less.

The fingers stop at a depth of groove. Mine did not stop at the sixth to the ninth, and I know words now that I did not read, and I know them the way the brothers said: afterward, as one knows a word one has just said. I have forgotten the names of the brothers who carried the eleven up. I had them. I had written them for the foot of this page, and I have looked at the place, and it is [ … ] and [ … ] and [ … ]. I cannot bring my teacher's face up. I can bring up his hands.

It may be that the reconstruction is them, thinking through me. A thought that has lost its head looks for a head, and a reader opens his, and reading is a wound. It may be that the end they describe is not coming. It may be that it is being written, and has been, since the first brother put his fingers in the first groove, and that what is writing it is not

[indent][i][color=#c8bfae][Here the Reliquarist's hand stops in the middle of the leaf. Beneath, in the hand of a brother of the Citadel: He was found at his table with his fingers in the grooves of the eleventh. He is well. He eats. He does not know us. Each morning he asks whose the pages are, and we tell him, and he reads them again, to the same place. We have put the fragments back in their box. There are twelve.][/color][/i][/indent]

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— a Reliquarist of the Citadel, who asked that his name be left off, and whose name the brothers have left off, since none of them has it now[/color][/i][/right]

pages.title: What He Said the Third Time
pages.by: Given me three times, at three fires, by the one every town has its own name for, and different each time; this is the third. I did not watch him write it, and I will not say where I was standing.
pages.bb:
[DRAFT] [font_size=30][color=#dcd3c2]What He Said the Third Time[/color][/font_size]

You want the end. Everyone who sits down here wants the end; nobody wants the middle, which is where you are sitting. Very well. It ends when Old Upright sets it down. The frame goes slack … the Hide comes off her like a cloth off a loom, and everything on it that has finished lies still, and everything that has not goes up. You will go up. You have never finished anything in your life. Neither have I. We will have company.

No. That is the Order's end, and the Order has never seen a thing end. It has seen things stop moving, and counted them. It ends when the mouth shuts. That paleness up there … the Lady of Bones is not lowering a cloth. The Guest Who Is Late is closing a door from the inside, and the ones who climbed are in the house, and you are on the step with your bowl held out to a door. I have stood on that step. The bowl was heavier when I put it down.

Or there is no mouth. Grandmother Spindle has her arm in the Hollow to the elbow, and one winter she pulls it out, and everything she ever drew through comes with it … every thread, every face, at every door in every valley at once, asking which way. That is the end: the lanes full of the dead and no one left to say which way, and the glass filling, and then the glass full, and nothing moving in it, and a candle that does not burn down. A still winter. Nothing to thaw. I have seen a small one. It was the quietest thing I have heard.

Or the Open Side closes. … The Glutton. No. I will be kind tonight: Our Lady of the Open Side. She fills the room you are sitting in. Every hollow: your mouth, the cup, the grave, the gap between one word and the one after it. There is no then after that, because then is a hollow too. You will not notice it end. Noticing needs somewhere to stand. Her brothers have poured a thousand years to bring it on, and they are the only house on the road that will get what it asked for.

Or it is paper. The Sigh Under the Door folds the Hide down the spine, head down, arms out … and cuts along the roads, and stands it on a step with its arms open, and nobody comes at dusk to breathe on it. You are a crease in it. You were always a crease in it. So was I, which is how I know where the folds are.

Or the Quiet finishes what it was saying. … I have heard the sentence. Not all of it; a word here, at a ford, at a fire, in a woodcutter's mouth between one breath and the next. The part I heard had your name in it, once, and I have not heard it since. The Unnaming is not cruel. Cruel takes trouble. It is finishing a sentence the way you finish a cup, because the cup is there and the hand is already round it.

Or there is a thought, far down, under the valves, in the dark that is the inside of a head, and it is thinking the Hide, and it has forgotten whose it is. One day it forgets you. That is the end for you. The rest goes on, in the thought, remembered by no one, and you were never there. It has forgotten me twice. I came back. I will not say how. I will say that the second time was easier, and that I did not like that it was.

Or none of the houses. Or the one who counts what is not his comes to the Hide and finds the column wrong, and takes the difference, and the difference is us. Or the Ferryman at the Dry Ford has his last fare, and it is yours, and he takes you across. Across what, I have not asked; I have paid him twice and sat in the boat and we did not go anywhere, and both times I was somewhere else when I stood up. Or the one who walks up the road the wrong way, from the gate of the Descent to the Cheek, since before the Breath, reaches the Cheek, and lies down, and so does everyone. Or the book on the stand in the ruin runs out of pages a page ahead of you. I have seen that book. The page ahead was not blank. I did not turn it.

Or it has ended. … You are reading this. The ink is dry. The fire I wrote it at is out, and I am not sitting at it, and you cannot be sure I ever was, and the end of a thing is when there is no one left at it to say it has not ended. Ask the fire.

Ask me again, another night, and I will tell you another. Not because I lie. I have been at the end of a great many things, more than you would credit, and not one of them ended the same way twice, and I have stopped expecting the last one to be tidier than the rest. The houses each chose. It is the one thing they have in common, and the one thing I will not do with them. Lower the wick. Pick one if you need one in your hand to sleep. I have not picked. I am still at the fire. Which of these that proves, you may decide, and I will not be here when you do.

[right][i][color=#c9974a]— [No name. Where one would go the leaf is worn through, as if a thumb had rested on the place a long while. The first time he gave me this it was a page longer. The second time it was two.][/color][/i][/right]
